propositions.text: Fengling Xu, Min Jin Yang, and their son sought protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: Fengling Xu and Min Jin Yang are a married couple. Jie Tao Yang is their son. All three have sought protection in Canada under sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 [IRPA].

propositions.text: Ms. Xu fears persecution in China as a Falun Gong practitioner and due to family planning practices.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu claims to fear persecution in China, her country of nationality, because she is a Falun Gong practitioner and because of that country’s oppressive family planning practices.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang fears persecution in Guyana due to his ethnicity and claims protection as a person in need.
propositions.quote: Mr. Yang is a citizen of China as well but he is also a citizen of Guyana. He claims to fear persecution in Guyana and that he is a person in need of protection because of his ethnicity.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and son make similar claims regarding Guyana; Mr. Yang also claims protection related to China as spouse of Falun Gong practitioner.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu and their son make similar claims with respect to Guyana. Mr. Yang also sought protection vis-à-vis China as the spouse of a Falun Gong practitioner.

propositions.text: All three applicants relied on Ms. Xu's personal narrative to support their protection claims.
propositions.quote: All three applicants relied on the personal narrative submitted by Ms. Xu in support of their claims for protection.

paragraphs.summary: The applicants, Xu family, seek protection in Canada under IRPA, alleging persecution in China and Guyana, relying on Ms. Xu's narrative.

propositions.text: The RPD heard the claims jointly on May 4, 2017, and rejected them on May 24, 2017.
propositions.quote: The claims were heard jointly by the Refugee Protection Division [RPD] of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada [IRB] on May 4, 2017. In a decision dated May 24, 2017, the RPD rejected the claims under both sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

propositions.text: RPD found applicants' identities and nationalities established.
propositions.quote: The RPD member was satisfied that the applicants had established their personal identities and nationalities.

propositions.text: RPD found discrimination against Chinese in Guyana but not persecution or need for protection for Mr. Yang; risk was generalized violence.
propositions.quote: with respect to Mr. Yang, the member concluded that, while there is some discrimination against Chinese people in Guyana, it did not rise to the level of persecution, nor would circumstances there cause Mr. Yang to be a person in need of protection. At most, he faced a generalized risk of violence.

propositions.text: RPD found Ms. Xu and son excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of Refugee Convention as they had access to Guyanese rights.
propositions.quote: with respect to Ms. Xu and her son, the member concluded that, because they “had access to the rights of nationals of Guyana,” they fell within Article 1E of the United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, 189 UNTS 150 [Refugee Convention] and, therefore, were excluded from refugee protection in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD found no basis to exempt Ms. Xu and son from Article 1E exclusion, applying same findings as for Mr. Yang.
propositions.quote: The member also concluded that there was no basis to exempt them from the application of Article 1E of the Refugee Convention because his findings with respect to Mr. Yang’s claim applied equally to them.

propositions.text: RPD did not address allegations regarding China for Ms. Xu and son.
propositions.quote: The member therefore did not address any of the allegations with respect to China.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the claims, finding identity established, no persecution for Mr. Yang in Guyana, and exclusion of Ms. Xu and son under Article 1E.

propositions.text: Applicants appealed to the RAD without new evidence or hearing request.
propositions.quote: The applicants appealed this decision to the Refugee Appeal Division [RAD] of the IRB. They did not file any new evidence or request a hearing.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed the RPD decision and dismissed the appeal on January 29, 2018.
propositions.quote: In a decision dated January 29, 2018, the RAD confirmed the decision of the RPD and dismissed the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants appealed to RAD, which confirmed RPD's decision and dismissed the appeal without new evidence or hearing.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD denied procedural fairness by deciding state protection issue without notice or opportunity to address it.
propositions.quote: They submit that the RAD denied them procedural fairness when it decided the issue of state protection against them without first giving them notice that this issue was in play or an opportunity to address it.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RAD's findings on lack of nexus to Convention ground, nature of risk in Guyana, and Article 1E exclusion are unreasonable.
propositions.quote: They also submit that the RAD’s determinations with respect to the lack of nexus to a Convention ground, with respect to the nature of the risk they face in Guyana, and with respect to exclusion under Article 1E of the Refugee Convention, are unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD denied procedural fairness and made unreasonable findings on nexus, risk, and Article 1E exclusion.

propositions.text: Court allows judicial review application, finds RAD's Article 1E exclusion determination unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I am satisfied that the RAD’s determination with respect to Article 1E exclusion is unreasonable.

propositions.text: Court finds RAD breached procedural fairness in considering state protection issue.
propositions.quote: I am also satisfied that the RAD’s consideration of the issue of state protection breached the requirements of procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Court orders a new hearing as a result.
propositions.quote: As a result, a new hearing is required.

paragraphs.summary: Court allows judicial review, finds RAD's Article 1E exclusion unreasonable and procedural fairness breached, orders new hearing.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu born in China July 1977; Mr. Yang born China November 1975; son born China August 2003; all Chinese nationals by birth.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu was born in China in July 1977. Mr. Yang was born there in November 1975. Their son Jie Tao was born there in August 2003. All three are Chinese nationals by birth.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Xu, Mr. Yang, and their son were born in China and are Chinese nationals by birth.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang left China in February 2004 to work in Guyana and support family.
propositions.quote: In February 2004, Mr. Yang left China to work in Guyana and support the family.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Yang left China in 2004 to work in Guyana and support the family.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu claims medical problems in China due to family planning practices; joined husband in Guyana in December 2010; son stayed with grandparents.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu claims that after their son was born she faced a number of medical problems in China as a result of Chinese family planning practices and requirements. Eventually, in December 2010 she decided to join her husband in Guyana. Their son remained behind with his grandparents in China.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Xu claims medical problems from family planning in China, joined husband in Guyana in 2010; son stayed in China.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang granted Guyanese citizenship May 2013; bought restaurant; both worked there; restaurant robbed twice; decided to sell and leave Guyana.
propositions.quote: In May 2013, Mr. Yang was granted Guyanese citizenship. That same month, he bought a restaurant in Georgetown, Guyana. Both he and Ms. Xu worked there. According to Ms. Xu’s narrative, the restaurant was robbed at gunpoint twice – the first time on December 10, 2013; the second time on May 5, 2014. In the first robbery, a gun was put to Ms. Xu’s head and she was assaulted. Shots were fired in the second robbery. After the second robbery, Ms. Xu and Mr. Yang decided to sell the restaurant and leave Guyana.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu left for China June 16, 2014; Mr. Yang stayed to sell restaurant.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu left for China on June 16, 2014. Mr. Yang stayed behind to sell the restaurant.

paragraphs.summary: Mr. Yang got Guyanese citizenship, bought restaurant, faced robberies; couple decided to sell and leave; Ms. Xu left in 2014, Mr. Yang stayed.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu faced continued family planning difficulties in China; took up Falun Gong; group session raided; she escaped and hid.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu claims that her difficulties with Chinese family planning practices and requirements continued after she returned to China. On the advice of a cousin, she took up the practice of Falun Gong as a way to deal with these difficulties. However, on August 31, 2014, a Falun Gong group session in which she was participating was raided by the Public Security Bureau [PSB]. Ms. Xu was able to make her escape and went into hiding.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu arranged with smuggler to leave China for US with son; met Mr. Yang in Seattle Feb 2015; all entered Canada irregularly near Vancouver; claimed refugee status in Toronto.
propositions.quote: Upon learning that the PSB were searching for her, Ms. Xu made arrangements with a smuggler to leave China for the United States with her son. The two of them met up with Mr. Yang in Seattle, Washington, in February 2015. They then all entered Canada irregularly near Vancouver. They submitted their refugee claims in Toronto approximately one month later.

paragraphs.summary: Ms. Xu took up Falun Gong, fled China with son after police raid, met Mr. Yang in US, then entered Canada irregularly and claimed refugee status.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and Mr. Yang submitted Basis of Claim Forms relying on Ms. Xu's narrative; each raised distinct claims regarding China and Guyana.
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu and Mr. Yang each submitted a Basis of Claim Form and other required documents but both relied on the information set out in Ms. Xu’s narrative. While the factual basis for the claims was advanced in common, each of the applicants raised distinct claims vis-à-vis China and Guyana.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu's narrative summarized fears: arrest and abuse in China for Falun Gong, forced IUD, son's safety, Mr. Yang fears criminals in Guyana and China due to Falun Gong.
propositions.quote: Their respective claims are summarized concisely in the following paragraph from Ms. Xu’s narrative: In China I fear arrest, imprisonment and abuse by the authorities because of my being a Falun Gong practitioner. I also fear being forced to wear an IUD against my will which I am against. In terms of my son, I fear for his safety as well because of my practice of Falun Gong. My husband too fears living in Guyana where he is worried that he will again be targeted by criminals and gangsters. It is similarly not safe for him to live in China because of my being a Falun Gong practitioner. For these reasons we are all seeking refugee protection in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants submitted claims relying on Ms. Xu's narrative, alleging fears of persecution in China and Guyana related to Falun Gong and family planning.

propositions.text: Applicants' counsel filed written submissions after RPD hearing, focusing on identity, credibility, and exclusion regarding Guyana.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the applicants filed written submissions shortly after the hearing before the RPD. Counsel continued to rely on all the grounds identified in Ms. Xu’s narrative. The legal submissions were framed around three specific issues: (1) identity; (2) credibility; and (3) exclusion (“ability of wife and minor son to get status in Guyana”).

propositions.text: RPD member had no different view of material issues than applicants' submissions.
propositions.quote: There is no suggestion in the RPD member’s reasons that he had a different view of what the material issues in the case were.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants' counsel submitted on identity, credibility, and exclusion; RPD member shared same view of material issues.

propositions.text: RPD member satisfied identity established but rejected claims under IRPA sections 96 and 97, limiting analysis to Guyana claims.
propositions.quote: As noted, the RPD member was satisfied that identity had been established. However, the member rejected the claims under both sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA. He limited his analysis to the claims vis-à-vis Guyana.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found identity established but rejected claims under IRPA, focusing only on Guyana claims.

propositions.text: RPD accepted restaurant robberies occurred but found no future risk engaging IRPA sections 96 or 97 for Mr. Yang.
propositions.quote: With respect to Mr. Yang, the member evidently accepted that the restaurant robberies had occurred but found that they were not indicative of a future risk that would engage either section 96 or 97.

propositions.text: RPD found risk related to restaurant ownership, now sold; no suggestion claimants couldn't live safely in other employment.
propositions.quote: Even if the robberies were “precipitated by” the claimants’ ethnicity, the member found that the risk “was still in relation to the claimants’ restaurant which has now been sold.” In the member’s view, there was “no suggestion or allegation that the claimants would be unable to live safely in Guyana in another employment capacity other than as restaurant owners.”

propositions.text: RPD found some discrimination against ethnic Chinese in Guyana but not persecution; risk was general crime risk; no findings on state protection.
propositions.quote: The member also found that while there is some discrimination against ethnic Chinese in Guyana, it did not rise to the level of persecution nor would Mr. Yang be exposed to anything more than a general risk of being a victim of crime there. The member did not make any findings with respect to state protection.

paragraphs.summary: RPD accepted robberies but found no persecution or future risk for Mr. Yang; risk limited to restaurant ownership; no state protection findings.

propositions.text: RPD found Federal Court of Appeal decision in Tretsetsang determinative for Ms. Xu and son.
propositions.quote: With respect to Ms. Xu and her son, the member found that the decision of the Federal Court of Appeal in Tretsetsang v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FCA 175 [Tretsetsang], was “determinative.”

propositions.text: RPD found Ms. Xu and son had access to Guyanese citizenship rights and made no reasonable efforts to obtain citizenship.
propositions.quote: In the member’s view, “Guyanese citizenship is within the control of the wife and child, and whereas they have not made any attempts to secure Guyanese citizenship, the panel finds that they have not made any reasonable efforts to overcome whatever impediments there may be, if any would even exist.”

propositions.text: RPD concluded Ms. Xu and son excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of Refugee Convention.
propositions.quote: On this basis, the member concluded that Ms. Xu and her son “have access to the rights of nationals of Guyana as contemplated in Article 1E of the Refugee Convention and they are excluded from refugee consideration in Canada.”

propositions.text: RPD found neither IRPA section 96 nor 97 engaged for Ms. Xu and son regarding Guyana; no evidence of Falun Gong persecution or forced IUD in Guyana.
propositions.quote: Further, the member found that neither sections 96 nor 97 of the IRPA was engaged with respect to Ms. Xu and her son vis-à-vis Guyana. The member applied the same findings as he made with respect to Mr. Yang’s claim and added: “There was no suggestion and no evidence that Falun Gong practitioners are persecuted in Guyana, nor that the wife would be required to wear an IUD in Guyana.” (To be sure, Ms. Xu’s claim for protection was never advanced on this basis.)

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Ms. Xu and son excluded under Article 1E due to access to Guyanese citizenship rights; no persecution or IRPA engagement found.

propositions.text: Applicants' appeal to RAD focused on three issues: nexus to Convention ground for Mr. Yang, generalized risk in Guyana, and Article 1E exclusion for Ms. Xu and son.
propositions.quote: In their written submissions in support of the appeal, the applicants identified and directed their submissions to the following three issues: a) Did the RPD err in finding that there is no nexus between Mr. Yang’s fear and a Convention ground? b) Did the RPD err in finding that Mr. Yang only faces a generalized risk in Guyana? c) Did the RPD err in finding that Ms. Xu and Jie Tao are excluded from protection pursuant to Article 1E of the Refugee Convention?

paragraphs.summary: Applicants appealed to RAD arguing errors on nexus, risk, and Article 1E exclusion issues.

propositions.text: Minister did not participate in the appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister did not participate in the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: Minister did not participate in the appeal.

propositions.text: RAD member applied correctness standard to RPD findings of fact and mixed fact and law, per Huruglica and X (Re).
propositions.quote: the RAD member instructed himself in accordance with the decision of the Federal Court of Appeal in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Huruglica, 2016 FCA 93 [Huruglica] as well as the decision of the three member RAD panel in X (Re), 2017 CanLII 33034 (CA IRB). As the member understood these authorities, with respect to findings of fact and mixed fact and law he was “to review the RPD decisions applying the correctness standard.

propositions.text: RAD may apply reasonableness standard if RPD has meaningful advantage, modified for RAD context.
propositions.quote: the RAD will normally apply a standard of correctness to all the findings of the RPD but where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage over the RAD in making a particular finding, the RAD may assess that finding using a standard of reasonableness, modified to suit the RAD context.

propositions.text: None of the grounds of appeal were decided on reasonableness standard; credibility was not an issue.
propositions.quote: As it happened, none of the grounds of appeal were determined on this basis. Credibility was not an issue.

paragraphs.summary: RAD applied correctness standard to RPD findings per Huruglica; reasonableness standard not applied; credibility not at issue.

propositions.text: RAD dismissed the appeal for reasons set out in following paragraphs.
propositions.quote: The RAD dismissed the appeal for the following reasons.

paragraphs.summary: RAD dismissed the appeal for reasons explained below.

propositions.text: RAD found RPD's statement on robberies less clear but rejected applicants' claim of ethnic risk in Guyana.
propositions.quote: while the RAD found that the RPD member’s statement that “[e]ven if the robberies were precipitated by the claimants’ ethnicity, it was still in relation to the claimants’ restaurant which has now been sold” was less clear than it could have been, the RAD rejected the applicants’ contention that they were at risk in Guyana, whether they were restaurant owners or not, because of their ethnicity.

propositions.text: RAD reviewed documentary evidence on Guyana country conditions and concluded applicants failed to establish well-founded fear on Convention ground.
propositions.quote: The RAD member conducted his own review of the documentary evidence before the RPD regarding country conditions in Guyana and concluded that the applicants had failed to establish a well-founded fear that they would be targeted on a Convention ground.

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD that applicants failed to establish nexus between fears and Convention ground.
propositions.quote: In short, the RAD agreed with the RPD that the applicants had failed to establish a nexus between their fears and a Convention ground.

paragraphs.summary: RAD found RPD's statement unclear but rejected ethnic risk claim; concluded applicants failed to establish nexus to Convention ground.

propositions.text: RAD member found applicants' fear of crime is a general risk in Guyana, not personal risk
propositions.quote: the applicants’ fear of crime “is a risk faced generally by others in Guyana”

propositions.text: Applicants did not rebut presumption that state protection is not available in Guyana
propositions.quote: applicants had “not rebutted the presumption that state protection is not [sic] available to them in Guyana.”

propositions.text: RAD agreed with RPD that evidence does not support applicants were targeted due to Chinese ethnicity
propositions.quote: evidence does not support the Appellants’ allegations that they were specifically targeted by criminals in Guyana because of their Chinese ethnicity

propositions.text: RAD agreed protection is not available to applicants in Guyana
propositions.quote: protection is not available to them.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member found applicants' fear of crime is a general risk in Guyana, did not rebut presumption of no state protection, and agreed with RPD on no specific targeting or protection availability.

propositions.text: RAD member agreed with RPD that Mr. Yang is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E
propositions.quote: he agreed with the assessment of the RPD that Mr. Yang “is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E”

propositions.text: RAD member found Ms. Xu and her son have access to rights of Guyana nationals and are excluded from refugee consideration
propositions.quote: [Ms. Xu and her son] have access to the rights of nationals of Guyana as contemplated in Article 1E of the Convention and they are excluded from refugee consideration in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member agreed with RPD that Mr. Yang is excluded under Article 1E and found Ms. Xu and her son have rights in Guyana and are excluded from refugee consideration.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed RPD decision under section 111(1)(a) of IRPA and dismissed appeal
propositions.quote: the RAD confirmed the decision of the RPD under section 111(1)(a) of the IRPA and dismissed the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirmed the RPD decision and dismissed the appeal under IRPA section 111(1)(a).

propositions.text: RAD's factual and mixed fact-law determinations reviewed on reasonableness standard
propositions.quote: The RAD’s determinations of factual issues and issues of mixed fact and law are reviewed on a reasonableness standard (Huruglica at para 35).

propositions.text: Reasonableness review concerns substantive outcome and reasoning process
propositions.quote: Reasonableness review “is concerned with the reasonableness of the substantive outcome of the decision, and with the process of articulating that outcome”

propositions.text: Reviewing court examines justification, transparency, intelligibility, and range of acceptable outcomes
propositions.quote: The reviewing court examines the decision for “the existence of justification, transparency and intelligibility within the decision-making process” and determines “whether the decision falls within a range of possible, acceptable outcomes which are defensible in respect of the facts and law”

propositions.text: Reasons must allow court to understand decision and determine if conclusion is acceptable
propositions.quote: the reasons allow the reviewing court to understand why the tribunal made its decision and permit it to determine whether the conclusion is within the range of acceptable outcomes”

propositions.text: Court should intervene only if criteria not met; not to reweigh evidence or substitute view
propositions.quote: The reviewing court should intervene only if these criteria are not met. It is not the role of the reviewing court to reweigh the evidence or to substitute its own view of a preferable outcome

paragraphs.summary: The RAD's factual and mixed fact-law decisions are reviewed for reasonableness, focusing on outcome and reasoning, with limited court intervention.

propositions.text: No standard of review for procedural fairness issues; court decides fairness itself
propositions.quote: if the issue is whether there was a breach of procedural fairness before the RAD, no standard of review is engaged. Rather, the reviewing court must determine for itself whether the process the member followed satisfied the level of fairness required

paragraphs.summary: For procedural fairness breaches, the court determines fairness itself without applying a standard of review.

propositions.text: Is RAD's exclusion of applicants under Article 1E unreasonable?
propositions.quote: Is the RAD’s determination that the applicants are excluded from refugee protection in Canada because of Article 1E of the Refugee Convention unreasonable?

propositions.text: Did RAD deny procedural fairness by deciding state protection issue without notice or opportunity to respond?
propositions.quote: Did the RAD deny the applicants procedural fairness by deciding the issue of state protection against them without first giving them notice that this issue was in play or an opportunity to address it?

propositions.text: Is RAD's conclusion that applicants failed to establish well-founded fear of persecution unreasonable?
propositions.quote: Is the RAD’s conclusion that the applicants failed to establish that they had a well-founded fear of persecution in Guyana unreasonable?

propositions.text: Is RAD's conclusion that applicants failed to establish need for protection unreasonable?
propositions.quote: Is the RAD’s conclusion that the applicants failed to establish that they were persons in need of protection in Guyana unreasonable?

paragraphs.summary: The court frames four issues: reasonableness of RAD's Article 1E exclusion, procedural fairness denial, and reasonableness of fear of persecution and need for protection findings.

propositions.text: Applicants did not present grounds in this order; first two issues are determinative; others need not be addressed
propositions.quote: I have found the first two of these issues to be determinative of this application. It is therefore not necessary to address the other two issues.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the first two issues determinative and will not address the other two.

propositions.text: Reviewing the role of the RAD before addressing grounds of judicial review
propositions.quote: Before addressing the grounds of judicial review set out above, it may be helpful to review the role of the RAD briefly.

paragraphs.summary: The court will briefly review the RAD's role before analyzing the judicial review grounds.

propositions.text: Section 110(1) IRPA allows appeal to RAD on law, fact, or mixed questions from RPD decisions
propositions.quote: Section 110(1) of the IRPA provides that a person or the Minister “may appeal... to the Refugee Appeal Division against a decision of the Refugee Protection Division

propositions.text: Section 110(2) IRPA limits appeals in certain cases but no other ground limitations where appeal exists
propositions.quote: Section 110(2) provides that there is no appeal to the RAD in certain classes of cases; however, where there is a right of appeal to the RAD, no other limitations are placed on the grounds of appeal

paragraphs.summary: IRPA sections 110(1) and (2) allow appeals to RAD on law, fact, or mixed questions with some exceptions but no other ground limits.

propositions.text: Section 110(3) IRPA requires RAD appeals proceed without hearing on RPD record
propositions.quote: Section 110(3) of the IRPA provides that generally an appeal to the RAD “must proceed without a hearing, on the basis of the record of the proceedings of the Refugee Protection Division.”

propositions.text: Sections 110(4)-(6) IRPA allow exceptions for new evidence and hearings with conditions
propositions.quote: Sections 110(4) and (5)... create an exception to this general rule. So too does section 110(6), which permits the RAD to hold a hearing provided certain preconditions are met.

propositions.text: FCA in Singh explained restrictions on new evidence preserve process integrity and finality
propositions.quote: placing restrictions on the admissibility of new evidence on appeal helps to preserve the integrity of the process by promoting finality with respect to the factual record at the first level of decision-making

paragraphs.summary: IRPA generally requires RAD appeals proceed without hearing on RPD record, with exceptions for new evidence and hearings to preserve finality.

propositions.text: RAD appeal is not a true de novo proceeding; it reviews RPD decision on record
propositions.quote: An appeal to the RAD is not a true de novo proceeding (Huruglica at para 79). The RAD conducts an appeal of the RPD’s decision, which is the initial point of reference.

propositions.text: RAD must carefully consider RPD decision and conduct own analysis to determine RPD error
propositions.quote: After “carefully considering” the RPD’s decision, the RAD should carry out “its own analysis of the record to determine whether, as submitted by the appellant, the RPD erred”

paragraphs.summary: The RAD reviews the RPD decision on the record, carefully considering and analyzing for errors, not a de novo hearing.

propositions.text: RAD has broad mandate to correct errors of fact, law, or mixed fact and law by RPD
propositions.quote: The RAD has a broad mandate to intervene to correct any error of fact, law, or mixed fact and law made by the RPD

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD findings on correctness standard but may defer on credibility where RPD has advantage
propositions.quote: The RAD reviews the RPD’s findings on the standard of correctness, although it may defer to the RPD on credibility findings “where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage”

propositions.text: RAD may confirm, set aside and substitute, or refer back RPD decision under IRPA s 111(1) and (2)
propositions.quote: After considering the appeal, the RAD may confirm the determination of the RPD; it may set aside the determination of the RPD and substitute a determination... or it may refer the matter to the RPD for a redetermination

paragraphs.summary: The RAD can correct RPD errors, review on correctness standard, and confirm, substitute, or refer back decisions under IRPA.

propositions.text: RAD can confirm RPD decision on another basis but must respect natural justice and fairness
propositions.quote: If there is an error, the RAD can still confirm the decision of the RPD on another basis... this power must be exercised in accordance with the principles of natural justice and procedural fairness.

propositions.text: RAD must give notice and opportunity to parties before confirming on a new basis not framed by parties
propositions.quote: before confirming a decision of the RPD on a basis that cannot reasonably be said to stem from the issues as framed by the parties, the RAD must give the affected parties notice and an opportunity to make submissions

propositions.text: If RAD makes further substantive findings, it must give notice and opportunity to parties
propositions.quote: if the RAD chooses to take a frolic and venture into the record to make further substantive findings, it should give some sort of notice to the parties and give them an opportunity to make submissions

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must give notice and opportunity before confirming RPD decisions on new bases or making further substantive findings.

propositions.text: Article 1E excludes persons recognized as having rights and obligations of nationality in country of residence
propositions.quote: Article 1E of the Refugee Convention states: “This Convention shall not apply to a person who is recognized by the competent authorities of the country in which he has taken residence as having the rights and obligations which are attached to the possession of nationality in that country.”

paragraphs.summary: Article 1E excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights and obligations in their country of residence.

propositions.text: RAD member's conclusions on Article 1E are puzzling in two respects
propositions.quote: the RAD member’s conclusions with respect to the application of Article 1E in the present case are puzzling in at least two respects.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD member's conclusions on Article 1E puzzling in two respects.

propositions.text: RAD member finds Mr. Yang excluded under Article 1E, but RPD did not
propositions.quote: the RAD member is expressing agreement with the RPD member’s conclusion in this regard. However, the RPD member drew no such conclusion with respect to Mr. Yang.

propositions.text: Issue of Article 1E exclusion for Mr. Yang is a red herring; burden on him to show fear of persecution in both China and Guyana
propositions.quote: the issue of the applicability of Article 1E to Mr. Yang would appear to be a red herring. He was seeking refugee protection vis-à-vis two different countries of which he is a national

propositions.text: Under IRPA s 96(a), burden on claimant to show well-founded fear in all countries of nationality
propositions.quote: Under section 96(a) of the IRPA, the burden was on him to demonstrate a well-founded fear of persecution in relation to both of these countries of citizenship before he could seek asylum in Canada

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD's Article 1E exclusion of Mr. Yang puzzling and irrelevant; burden is on him to show fear in both countries under IRPA.

propositions.text: RAD member agrees with RPD that Ms. Xu and son excluded under Article 1E but RPD basis was erroneous
propositions.quote: the RPD member found that Ms. Xu and her son were excluded under Article 1E, he did so on what is clearly an erroneous basis.

propositions.text: RPD relied on Tretsetsang case which concerns IRPA s 96(a), not Article 1E
propositions.quote: the RPD member considered the decision of the Federal Court of Appeal in Tretsetsang to be “determinative on this point.” Tretsetsang, however, concerns the meaning of “each of their countries of nationality” in section 96(a) of the IRPA, not Article 1E of the Refugee Convention.

propositions.text: RAD member does not mention RPD's flawed analysis but conducts own analysis under Zeng
propositions.quote: The RAD member does not mention this flaw in the RPD’s analysis, although perhaps it is why he went on to conduct his own analysis under the proper test, as stated in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Zeng, 2010 FCA 118 [Zeng].

propositions.text: Court will explain why RAD's analysis is unreasonable
propositions.quote: As I will explain, however, that analysis is unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD's Article 1E exclusion basis erroneous, RAD did not address this flaw but did own analysis, which court finds unreasonable.

propositions.text: Zeng test for Article 1E exclusion involves status similar to nationals and balancing factors if status lost
propositions.quote: Considering all relevant factors to the date of the hearing, does the claimant have status, substantially similar to that of its nationals, in the third country?...

paragraphs.summary: The Zeng test for Article 1E exclusion asks if claimant has status similar to nationals; if lost, various factors must be balanced.

propositions.text: Court understands RAD member answered Zeng test questions in a certain way
propositions.quote: As I understand the RAD member’s reasons, he answered these questions in the following way.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains how it understands the RAD member answered the Zeng test questions.

propositions.text: RAD member found Ms. Xu and son did not have status substantially similar to nationals in Guyana at hearing
propositions.quote: neither Ms. Xu nor her son had status in Guyana substantially similar to that of its nationals at the time of the hearing.

propositions.text: Therefore, they were not excluded from refugee protection on this basis
propositions.quote: They were therefore not excluded from refugee protection on this basis.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member found Ms. Xu and son lacked status similar to nationals in Guyana and thus were not excluded from refugee protection on that basis.

propositions.text: RAD member could not conclude Ms. Xu and son had status but Ms. Xu had right to reside in Guyana then
propositions.quote: the RAD member was unable to conclude that Ms. Xu and her son ever had such status although it was clear that Ms. Xu (at least) had had a right to reside in Guyana during the time she was there.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member could not conclude Ms. Xu and her son had status but Ms. Xu had right to reside in Guyana then, court finds.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and son had access to status similar to Guyanese nationals between Dec 2010 and June 2014
propositions.quote: they did have access to status substantially similar to that of nationals of Guyana – in particular, when Ms. Xu was living there with Mr. Yang between December 2010 and June 2014

propositions.text: Ms. Xu aware she could apply for status but took no action to normalize it
propositions.quote: she was aware of her ability to apply for status in Guyana, but she took no action or made any attempt to normalize her status

propositions.text: Ms. Xu failed without good reason to preserve right to return to Guyana
propositions.quote: she failed “without good and sufficient reason” to preserve her right to be permitted to return to Guyana

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and son excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of Refugee Convention
propositions.quote: he concluded that Ms. Xu and her son were excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of the Refugee Convention

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found Ms. Xu and son had status access but took no action to normalize it and were excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E.

propositions.text: Applicants challenged RPD finding that Guyanese citizenship was within their control
propositions.quote: the applicants specifically took issue with the RPD member’s finding that Guyanese citizenship was “within the control” of Ms. Xu and her son

propositions.text: Canadian case law holds potential Guyanese citizenship not within spouse's control due to executive discretion
propositions.quote: Canadian case law dealing specifically with Guyana which holds that potential Guyanese citizenship is not “within the control” of the spouse of a Guyanese citizen because whether it is granted or not is determined by the Executive in the exercise of its discretion

propositions.text: Evidence suggested this remains true but RAD member did not address applicants' argument
propositions.quote: The evidence before the RAD suggested that this was still the case but the member does not address the applicants’ argument

paragraphs.summary: Applicants challenged RPD's control finding; case law says citizenship not within spouse's control; RAD did not address this argument, court notes.

propositions.text: Determinative issue is RAD's failure to consider Ms. Xu's explanation for not securing Guyana status
propositions.quote: the determinative issue here is the failure of the RAD member to engage in any meaningful way with Ms. Xu’s explanation for why she did not attempt to secure her status in Guyana

propositions.text: Ms. Xu left Guyana after two violent armed robberies and feared recurrence
propositions.quote: Ms. Xu left Guyana because she had been the victim of two violent armed robberies within less than six months. She feared being a victim again

propositions.text: Neither RPD nor RAD disbelieved Ms. Xu's account of events
propositions.quote: Neither the RPD nor the RAD member disbelieved Ms. Xu’s account of these events

propositions.text: Ms. Xu's explanation for losing status must be considered under Zeng but RAD did not do so
propositions.quote: Under Zeng, Ms. Xu’s explanation for why she lost her status in Guyana must be considered but the member never does so

propositions.text: RAD's exclusion conclusion under Article 1E lacks justification, transparency and intelligibility
propositions.quote: his conclusion that she is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of the Refugee Convention lacks justification, transparency and intelligibility

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RAD failed to consider Ms. Xu's explanation for status loss despite credible fear; exclusion under Article 1E lacks justification.

propositions.text: Applicants argued RPD erred on risk nexus and personalized risk under sections 96 and 97 IRPA
propositions.quote: applicants challenged the RPD’s determinations that any risk they faced in Guyana lacked a nexus to a Convention ground, as required by section 96 of the IRPA, and, further, that it did not rise to the level of a personalized risk, as required by section 97

propositions.text: RAD upheld RPD's determinations but relied on evidence about Guyana authorities' protection efforts
propositions.quote: the RAD relied on evidence in the record relating to efforts by the authorities in Guyana to protect ethnic Chinese there and made specific findings with respect to state protection

propositions.text: Applicants say procedural fairness breached as they had no notice or chance to address state protection issue
propositions.quote: applicants submit that this breached the duty of procedural fairness because they did not have notice that this issue was in play or an opportunity to make submissions with respect to it

propositions.text: Court agrees applicants were denied procedural fairness on state protection issue
propositions.quote: I agree with the applicants

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argued RPD erred on risk nexus and personalized risk; RAD relied on state protection evidence without notice; court agrees procedural fairness breached.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness requires notice and opportunity to address new issues before RAD confirms RPD decision on new basis
propositions.quote: the duty of procedural fairness requires that before the RAD confirms a decision of the RPD on a new basis, the party or parties to the appeal must be told that the issue is in play and given an opportunity make submissions on it

propositions.text: No dispute on principle or test for 'newness' of issue; disputes arise on application
propositions.quote: There does not appear to be any disagreement in the jurisprudence about this principle or about the test for “newness” – i.e. that the issue cannot reasonably be said to stem from the issues as framed by the parties

paragraphs.summary: Court states procedural fairness requires notice and opportunity on new issues; principle and test for newness undisputed; disputes arise on application.

propositions.text: Issue of state protection is new and did not stem from issues framed by parties
propositions.quote: I am satisfied that the issue of state protection is a new one in the requisite sense in this case

propositions.text: Claimants must approach home state for protection before other states' responsibility engaged (Ward)
propositions.quote: persecuted persons are required to approach their home state for protection before the responsibility of other states is engaged (Canada (Attorney General) v Ward, [1993] 2 SCR 689 at 709 [Ward])

propositions.text: Home state's inability to protect is crucial to well-founded fear (Ward)
propositions.quote: their home state’s inability to protect “is a crucial element in determining whether the claimant’s fear is well-founded” (Ward at 722)

propositions.text: State protection not identified as material issue before RPD; no submissions or determinations on it
propositions.quote: state protection was not identified as a material issue in this case at the hearing before the RPD, as a result the applicants’ written submissions to the RPD do not address it, and the RPD member did not make any determinations in relation to it

propositions.text: Applicants' appeal focused on lack of nexus; state protection issue never reached by RPD
propositions.quote: the applicants’ appeal was understandably – indeed, necessarily – directed to other issues. In particular, in relation to section 96, the issue was the RPD’s finding of a lack of nexus to a Convention ground

propositions.text: Applicants entitled to notice and opportunity on state protection issue before RAD decision
propositions.quote: they were entitled to be told that state protection was in play at the RAD and they should have had an opportunity to make submissions on it before the appeal was decided

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection issue is new, not raised before RPD, and applicants deserved notice and chance to address it before RAD decision.

propositions.text: Respondent argues state protection issue immaterial as alternative basis; outcome inevitable
propositions.quote: the respondent submits, in effect, that even if this is so, the issue of state protection is immaterial in this case because it is really only an alternative basis for upholding the RPD’s decision

propositions.text: RAD could have upheld lack of nexus and absence of personalized risk without state protection issue
propositions.quote: the RAD could have upheld the determinations of a lack of nexus and the absence of personalized risk without ever considering the issue of state protection

propositions.text: Some RAD reasons unrelated to state protection and free of reviewable error
propositions.quote: some of the reasons the RAD offered for upholding the RPD’s determinations have nothing whatsoever to do with state protection and those reasons are not tainted by any other reviewable error

propositions.text: Adverse outcome was legally inevitable
propositions.quote: an adverse outcome for the applicants was legally inevitable

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues state protection issue immaterial; RAD could uphold decision without it; adverse outcome was inevitable, respondent submits.

propositions.text: Court not persuaded breach of procedural fairness should be overlooked due to legal inevitability
propositions.quote: I am not persuaded that the breach of procedural fairness should be overlooked because the result in this case was legally inevitable

propositions.text: Court gives three main reasons for this view
propositions.quote: I say this for three main reasons

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects respondent's inevitability argument and gives three reasons for not overlooking procedural fairness breach.

propositions.text: Breach relates to Guyana claims but applicants also made claims vis-à-vis China not examined on merits
propositions.quote: the applicants had also made claims vis-à-vis China. These claims have never been examined on their merits

propositions.text: Erroneous exclusion under Article 1E prevented merits examination of China claims
propositions.quote: because of erroneous determinations ... that Ms. Xu was excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E

propositions.text: Court cannot say claims are doomed after proper consideration
propositions.quote: I am in no position to say that her claim for protection ... is doomed to fail in its entirety after proper consideration

paragraphs.summary: Court notes breach relates to Guyana claims but China claims remain unexamined due to erroneous exclusion; cannot say claims doomed.

propositions.text: State protection issue intertwined with RAD's section 97 determination
propositions.quote: I am not satisfied that the issue of state protection can safely be disentangled from the rest of the RAD member’s reasons in this case

propositions.text: RAD relied on presumption of state protection not rebutted by applicants without submissions
propositions.quote: The member expressly makes and relies upon the finding that the applicants have not rebutted the presumption that state protection is available to them in Guyana

propositions.text: Upholding result on respondent's basis would require rewriting RAD reasons, exceeding judicial review bounds
propositions.quote: To uphold the result on the basis advanced by the respondent would require fundamentally re-writing the member’s reasons, something that exceeds the proper bounds of judicial review

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection issue integral to RAD's section 97 reasons; rewriting reasons to uphold would exceed judicial review scope.

propositions.text: State protection important to RAD's section 96 reasons on nexus to Convention ground
propositions.quote: state protection is less prominent in the member’s discussion under section 96 of the IRPA, it is important nonetheless and relates directly to the issue of nexus with a Convention ground

propositions.text: RAD diminished probative value of applicants' news reports due to missing context of state protection efforts
propositions.quote: the probative value of information the applicants drew from two news reports ... was diminished because ... the missing context ... relating to efforts by the authorities in Guyana to provide additional assistance and protection

propositions.text: RPD did not rely on state protection information; applicants had no reason to address it before RAD decision
propositions.quote: The RPD member had not placed any reliance on this information. The applicants had no reason to think that its significance ... needed to be addressed until they received the RAD member’s reasons

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection issue important to RAD's nexus reasoning; applicants had no notice to address it before decision.

propositions.text: Applicants entitled to submissions opportunity on state protection issue; failure breached procedural fairness
propositions.quote: The applicants should have been given an opportunity to make submissions on this issue before the appeal was decided. The failure to do so resulted in a breach of procedural fairness

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes applicants were denied procedural fairness by not being given chance to address state protection issue.

propositions.text: Judicial review application allowed; RAD decision set aside; matter remitted for redetermination by different decision-maker
propositions.quote: the application for judicial review of the decision of the RAD dated January 29, 2018, is allowed, the decision is set aside, and the matter is remitted for redetermination by a different decision-maker

paragraphs.summary: Court allows judicial review, sets aside RAD decision, and remits matter for redetermination by different decision-maker.

propositions.text: No serious questions of general importance for certification under section 74(d) IRPA
propositions.quote: The parties did not suggest any serious questions of general importance for certification under section 74(d) of the IRPA. I agree that none arise

propositions.text: Judgment: judicial review allowed, RAD decision set aside, matter remitted, no question of general importance stated
propositions.quote: THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that The application for judicial review is allowed. The decision of the Refugee Appeal Division dated January 29, 2018, is set aside and the matter is remitted for redetermination by a different decision-maker. No question of general importance is stated

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no serious questions of general importance; judgment allows judicial review, sets aside RAD decision, remits matter.
